page.overview:
What is Apostle?

Each apostle is unique in their released form - a "proper form", according to Ubik. Their appearance varies greatly, from warped versions of animals to monstrosities, many of which bear remnants of their human features. Conversely, the features of an apostle's released form are often reflected in their normal form, ranging from the obvious, like Wyald's ape-like face, to the more human features of Locus, Grunbeld, and Irvine. The appearance of each apostle is often a reflection of their ego and desire, such as Rosine's physical resemblance to an elf after her fascination for them. Furthermore, it seems that the candidates have some power of choice as to what form they will be given: the Count wanted not to feel suffering and, when meeting the Idea of Evil, Griffith wished for wings.

When an apostle is killed, their spirit is dragged into the Abyss, and their physical body reverts back to its original normal form with all injuries remaining on their bodies analogous to the injured parts of their previous apostle form.

Refashioned by causality and extraordinary obsession, most apostles are defined by their lack of empathy and insatiable desire for bloodshed, though there are exceptionally disciplined apostles such as Locus, Grunbeld, and Irvine, who can suppress their ravenous tendencies. Following the Incarnation Ceremony, numerous apostles flock to Griffith and pledge their allegiance to him. In doing so, they are finally granted a place in the world of man, fighting alongside humanity as the White Falcon's metaphorical beaks and talons.

Despite their transmigration, several apostles retain at least part of their former humanity. Examples include:
